[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Teams need branch and merge conventions that support independent service releases without forcing a single release cadence across all components in a repository.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

Use short-lived change branches with trunk-oriented integration, then drive release isolation through service-scoped semantic tags and PR metadata practices rather than long-lived release branches.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- Independently deployable micro-service and micro-frontend delivery models
- Repository topologies where multiple release units share one source repository
- Federated poly-repository environments requiring consistent release branch conventions
- Teams adopting or migrating away from GitFlow or environment-based branching models
page_texts.7:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- Reduces branch divergence and merge conflict surface area
- Enables each service or component to release on its own cadence
- Produces auditable, immutable release cut points through scoped tags
- Aligns with trunk-based development practices recommended for CI/CD velocity
page_texts.9:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

Organizations delivering software as independently deployable services need to move quickly on individual components without coordinating a single global release. Regulatory and audit requirements also demand clear traceability between source changes, release artifacts, and deployment events for each bounded service.
page_texts.10:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

GitHub repositories hosting multiple services or components face a structural challenge: a single mainline branch does not, by itself, provide isolation between the release cycles of those components. Without an explicit convention, teams impose ad-hoc workarounds — environment branches, perpetual release branches, or manual tagging — each of which introduces divergence risk and inconsistent release traceability.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

Branching models designed for single-release-unit repositories apply one set of conventions to all components. When multiple services share a repository, any component merging a change must either wait for all other components to be ready (forced coupling) or maintain a proliferation of long-lived branches that diverge and conflict. Neither outcome supports high-frequency, independent delivery.
page_texts.12:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- Need rapid merge feedback and low branch divergence
- Need per-service release cut points and immutable traceability
- Need compatibility with both mono-repository and poly-repository topologies
- Need release automation that scopes notes, assets, and notifications per release unit
page_texts.14:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

1. Use short-lived feature branches (typically `feature/<id>-<description>`) merged frequently into a single protected mainline branch (`main`).
2. Protect `main` with branch policies requiring PR review and passing CI before merge.
3. Reserve release branches (`release/<service>/<version>`) only when a specific release unit requires a stabilization period prior to its production cut.
4. Express every production release as a service-scoped semantic tag: `<service>/v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` for mono-repositories, `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` for dedicated poly-repositories.
5. Attach PR labels and milestones that correspond to the releasing service/version so release notes can be generated per release unit from merged PR metadata.
page_texts.15:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#architecture-diagram]

### Architecture Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Main["main branch (protected, always deployable)"]
        direction LR
    end

    FeatureA["feature/123-add-auth"] -->|PR| Main
    FeatureB["feature/456-new-ui"] -->|PR| Main
    Main -->|optional stabilization| ReleaseBranch["release/service-a/1.4.0"]
    ReleaseBranch -->|hotfix merged back + tag| Main

    Main --> TagA["service-a/v1.4.0 (immutable)"]
    Main --> TagB["service-b/v2.1.0 (immutable)"]
    TagA --> CIA["CI produces release assets & notes for service-a only"]
    TagB --> CIB["CI produces release assets & notes for service-b only"]
```
page_texts.16:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mainline branch (`main`) | Single integration point; always kept in a deployable state | Branch protection rules, required CI checks |
| Short-lived feature branch | Isolated unit of work; merged via PR within days | Mainline branch |
| Service-scoped semantic tag | Immutable release cut point for a single release unit | Tagging convention, tag-triggered CI workflow |
| PR label / milestone | Associates a merged change with a specific service and release version | Label taxonomy, milestone naming convention |
| Release workflow | Generates scoped release notes and artifacts triggered by tag push | Tag naming convention, PR label taxonomy |
page_texts.17:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

1. A developer creates a short-lived feature branch from `main` and opens a PR.
2. CI runs on the PR; branch protection rules block merge until checks pass and a reviewer approves.
3. On merge to `main`, CI validates the integrated state; deployment to non-production environments may be triggered automatically.
4. When a release unit is ready, a team member creates a service-scoped tag (e.g., `service-a/v1.4.0`) from the desired `main` commit.
5. The tag push triggers a release workflow scoped to that service, which generates release notes from PRs labeled with `service-a` closed in the milestone `service-a-1.4.0`, builds release artifacts, and publishes a GitHub Release.
page_texts.18:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

- **Trunk-only (no release branches)**: All stabilization happens on `main`; release branches are never used. Applicable when all services in the repository deploy continuously from `main` with feature flags.
- **Release-branch stabilization**: A short-lived `release/<service>/<version>` branch is cut when a specific service requires a freeze period. Hotfixes land on the release branch and are cherry-picked back to `main`. The release tag is cut from the release branch tip.
- **Poly-repository (single release unit per repo)**: Each repository contains one release unit; tags follow `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` without a service prefix. Label scoping is not required.
page_texts.20:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#prerequisites]

### Prerequisites

- GitHub repository with branch protection enabled on `main`
- GitHub Actions or equivalent CI capable of triggering on tag push events
- Agreed label taxonomy identifying each release unit (e.g., `service-a`, `service-b`)
- Milestone naming convention aligned to service and version (e.g., `service-a-1.4.0`)
- Semantic versioning familiarity across contributing teams
page_texts.22:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#phase-1-branch-protection-and-ci-baseline]

#### Phase 1: Branch Protection and CI Baseline

1. Enable branch protection on `main` requiring at least one PR approval and passing status checks before merge.
2. Configure CI workflow triggered on `pull_request` and `push` to `main` to run build, lint, and test stages.
3. Establish the short-lived branch naming convention (`feature/`, `bugfix/`, `hotfix/`) and document it in the repository's `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
page_texts.23:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#phase-2-label-and-milestone-taxonomy]

#### Phase 2: Label and Milestone Taxonomy

1. Create a GitHub label for each release unit in the repository (e.g., `service-a`, `service-b`).
2. Define a milestone naming convention: `<service>-<version>` (e.g., `service-a-1.4.0`).
3. Require contributors to apply the appropriate service label and milestone when opening PRs that target a specific service release.
page_texts.24:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#phase-3-tag-triggered-release-workflow]

#### Phase 3: Tag-Triggered Release Workflow

1. Define the service-scoped tag convention: `<service>/v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` for mono-repositories.
2. Create a GitHub Actions release workflow triggered by `push` events matching `refs/tags/<service>/v*`.
3. Configure the workflow to filter closed PRs by label and milestone to generate scoped release notes.
4. Publish a GitHub Release from the tag, attaching release notes and any built artifacts.
page_texts.26:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#example-1-branch-protection-rule-github-ui--api]

#### Example 1: Branch Protection Rule (GitHub UI / API)

```yaml
# Branch protection for main (representative settings)
branch: main
required_pull_request_reviews:
  required_approving_review_count: 1
required_status_checks:
  strict: true
  contexts:
    - ci / build
    - ci / lint
    - ci / test
enforce_admins: true
allow_force_pushes: false
```
page_texts.27:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#example-2-tag-triggered-release-workflow]

#### Example 2: Tag-Triggered Release Workflow

```yaml
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - '*/v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+'   # matches service-a/v1.4.0, service-b/v2.1.0

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: read
    steps:
      - name: Extract service name from tag
        id: meta
        run: |
          TAG="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"          # e.g. service-a/v1.4.0
          echo "service=${TAG%%/v*}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "version=${TAG##*/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Generate release notes
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          SERVICE: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.service }}
          MILESTONE: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.service }}-${{ steps.meta.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          gh pr list --state merged --label "$SERVICE" --search "milestone:\"$MILESTONE\"" \
            --json title,number,url \
            --jq '.[] | "- " + .title + " (#" + (.number|tostring) + ")"' > release-notes.md

      - name: Publish GitHub Release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@3bb12739c298aeb8a4eeaf626c5b8d85266b0e65 # v2.6.2
        with:
          name: '${{ steps.meta.outputs.service }} ${{ steps.meta.outputs.version }}'
          body_path: release-notes.md
```
page_texts.28:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- Keep feature branches short-lived — target merge within one to three days to minimize divergence risk.
- Never commit directly to `main`; all changes flow through reviewed pull requests.
- Apply service labels and milestone assignments at PR open time, not at merge time, to maintain accurate release note generation.
- Cut release tags from a known-good `main` commit, not from a branch head, unless a stabilization branch is in use.
- Automate release note generation rather than authoring manually to ensure consistency and completeness.
page_texts.29:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- **Long-lived feature branches**: Extended isolation produces large diffs, conflicts, and delayed integration feedback. Use feature flags to merge incomplete work safely.
- **Missing label/milestone discipline**: PRs merged without correct labels and milestones will not appear in scoped release notes, breaking audit traceability.
- **Tag reuse or mutation**: Never move or delete a release tag after it has been published. Create a new patch version instead.
- **Release branches left open indefinitely**: Release branches intended for stabilization become a maintenance burden if not deleted after the release tag is cut.
page_texts.31:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#standards-alignment]

### Standards Alignment

- [ADR-TEC-015 Source Control Repository Management](../../../decisions/technology/ADR-TEC-015-source-control-repository-management.md) — establishes the enterprise mandate for GitHub as the source control platform and defines repository governance expectations that this pattern operationalizes at the branch and release level.
- [GUID-TEC-STRAT-003 GitHub Release Management Strategy](../../../strategy/guidance/technology/strategy/GUID-TEC-STRAT-003-github-release-management-strategy.md) — defines the enterprise release tagging and release note generation guidance that this pattern implements.
page_texts.32:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#compliance-requirements]

### Compliance Requirements

- Release tags must be immutable; tag deletion or mutation in a production-designated repository must generate an audit event.
- Each GitHub Release must link back to the set of merged PRs that constitute the release to satisfy change traceability obligations.
- Branch protection rules on `main` must be enforced for all repositories carrying production-destined code.
page_texts.33:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#approval-process]

### Approval Process

1. Teams adopting this pattern must document their label taxonomy and milestone convention in the repository `CONTRIBUTING.md` prior to the first tagged release.
2. The release workflow definition must be reviewed by the owning team's architecture representative before the first production release.
3. Significant deviations from the tag naming convention require an ADR update to ADR-TEC-015.
page_texts.34:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#monitoring-and-metrics]

### Monitoring and Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mean feature branch lifetime | ≤ 3 business days | GitHub Insights — average PR open-to-merge time |
| PR merge-to-main rate | 100% via PR (no direct commits) | Branch protection audit log |
| Release tag integrity | 0 deleted or mutated tags | Tag deletion webhook or audit log alert |
| Release note completeness | 100% of merged PRs attributed to a release | Diff between merged PRs and release-note PR set per release |
page_texts.36:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#real-world-example-1]

### Real-World Example 1

**Context:** A mono-repository hosting three independently deployed API services (auth, billing, notifications) that release on different weekly cadences.

**Implementation:** Each service has a corresponding GitHub label. Feature branches are merged to `main` continuously. When the billing team is ready to release `v2.3.0`, a team member creates tag `billing/v2.3.0` from the current `main` HEAD. The tag-triggered release workflow filters merged PRs labeled `billing` closed in milestone `billing-2.3.0` and publishes a GitHub Release with generated notes. The auth and notifications services are unaffected.

**Outcome:** Billing deploys independently; no coordination with other service teams is required. Release notes are complete and traceable to specific PRs.
page_texts.37:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#real-world-example-2]

### Real-World Example 2

**Context:** A poly-repository where each microservice owns its own GitHub repository and releases independently.

**Implementation:** Each repository uses a simplified convention — tags follow `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` without a service prefix. Branch protection and PR workflow are identical to the mono-repository variant. Release notes are generated from all PRs merged since the previous tag, since the entire repository represents one release unit.

**Outcome:** Consistent release practices across all service repositories with minimal ceremony.
page_texts.39:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#scenario-1-emergency-hotfix-during-active-release-stabilization]

#### Scenario 1: Emergency Hotfix During Active Release Stabilization

A critical defect is found while `service-a/v1.4.0` is being stabilized on a release branch. A hotfix PR is raised directly against the `release/service-a/1.4.0` branch, reviewed, and merged. The fix is immediately cherry-picked to `main` via a separate PR. The release tag is cut from the release branch tip after the fix is confirmed.
page_texts.40:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#scenario-2-coordinated-multi-service-release]

#### Scenario 2: Coordinated Multi-Service Release

Two services with a hard API contract dependency must release together. Both service labels are applied to the coordinating PRs. Tags `service-a/v2.0.0` and `service-b/v3.0.0` are cut in sequence within a planned maintenance window. Each release workflow runs independently but the dependency is documented in both release notes.
page_texts.42:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#before-problem-state]

#### Before (Problem State)

Three services share a mono-repository. Each team maintains a long-lived `release/service-X` branch. Changes frequently diverge; merge conflicts require dedicated resolution sprints. No automated release notes exist — change lists are assembled manually from commit messages. A defect in one service's release branch blocks all releases until resolved.
page_texts.43:
[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#after-solution-state]

#### After (Solution State)

All changes flow through short-lived feature branches merged to `main`. Each service releases independently by pushing a scoped tag. Release notes are generated automatically from labeled PR metadata. Teams are decoupled — a defect in `service-a`'s release does not affect `service-b`'s release cadence.

[patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-002-branch-merge-independent-release-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** Branch-only strategies designed for single-release-unit repositories unintentionally couple independently deployable services, forcing coordinated release cadences.

**Solution:** Keep branches short-lived and integrate frequently to a protected mainline; express independent releases through service-scoped semantic tags and PR label/milestone metadata that drive automated release note generation.

**When to Use:** Any GitHub-hosted repository delivering multiple independently deployable services or components, or any poly-repository environment requiring consistent release branch conventions.

**Key Benefits:**

- Eliminates forced release coupling between independent services
- Provides immutable, auditable release cut points through scoped tags
- Automates release note generation with full PR traceability
- Scales from single-service poly-repositories to complex mono-repositories

**Implementation Complexity:** Medium

**Prerequisites:** GitHub repository with branch protection on `main`, agreed label taxonomy per release unit, and a tag-triggered CI release workflow.

**Related Patterns:** PTN-TECH-GOV-001 (Golden Path CI/CD Pipeline), PTN-TECH-GOV-003 (SubTree/Submodule Integration)
